title: footprint.overlap 1.0.0
description: The fourth result of a footprint run: which open pull requests touch a file this change touches, the conflict graph between the open pull requests, and a proposed merge order as waves. Every figure comes from gh pr list --json and gh pr diff --name-only; when gh cannot answer, available is false and the reason is stated rather than the section being omitted.

range.description: The git range whose files were compared against the open pull requests

available.description: False when gh is absent, unauthenticated, rate-limited or unreadable; the section is stated, never omitted

code.description: Why the overlap is unavailable; present only when available is false

reason.description: gh's own message, or why gh could not be found

summary.description: The plain statement: the counts, or that there is no overlap, or the limitation. Never an empty section.

self.description: The pull request under review: the open pull request whose head commit is the range's head commit, or, when no head commit matches, the same-repository pull request whose head branch is the range's head branch. Excluded from overlapping and kept in the waves; always present, null when none matches.

openPullRequests.description: How many open pull requests gh listed

truncated.description: True when the list came back at the limit, so there may be more open pull requests than were considered

overlapping.description: Open pull requests that change a file this change changes, ascending by number

conflicts.description: One edge per pair of open pull requests that change the same file, with the files named

reason.description: Why the edge exists, in prose

waves.description: The proposed merge order. No two pull requests in a wave share a file; wave N+1 lands after wave N. Greedy first-fit, so a proposal rather than a minimum.

undetermined.description: Open pull requests whose changed files gh would not report. Kept out of the conflict graph and the waves rather than assumed disjoint.

digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of range and overlap (spec §7.1). Unlike inv, it moves with the live state of the open pull requests.
